mainTopic: The four fasts of זכריה: when they apply, which dates they mark, and whether the happy days of מגילת תענית were cancelled
overview: The גמרא brings רבי שמעון חסידא's explanation of זכריה 8:19, which calls the same four days both fasts and days of joy: it depends on whether there is peace. רב פפא adds that when there is neither persecution nor peace, fasting is optional, but תשעה באב stays required because so many disasters happened on it. A ברייתא then brings רבי עקיבא's identification of the four fasts: ט׳ בתמוז, תשעה באב, ג׳ תשרי (the killing of גדליה), and עשרה בטבת. רבי שמעון disagrees about the fast of the tenth. He says it is ה׳ בטבת, the day the news of the destruction reached the exiles, so the list follows the order of the disasters. Next, אמוראים argue whether the happy days of מגילת תענית were cancelled after the חורבן. רב כהנא challenges from a fast decreed on חנוכה, and רב יוסף answers that חנוכה is different because its miracle is well known. Finally, רב אחא בר הונא challenges from a day that was added to מגילת תענית later, and the גמרא answers that it was added while the בית המקדש still stood.

steps.title: A verse that calls the same days both fasts and joyful days
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא quotes זכריה 8:19 and points out that the פסוק calls the four days both 'fast' and 'joy and gladness.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חנא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: What does the פסוק mean, 'Thus said ה׳ of hosts: The fast of the fourth, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth shall be for the house of Judah for joy and gladness'? It calls them 'fast,' and it also calls them 'joy and gladness'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a statement that sets up a puzzle in a פסוק. The same four days are called both 'fasts' and 'joyful days.' The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is a contradiction inside one פסוק: a day cannot be a fast and a celebration at the same time. Pointing out this tension sets up the rule that the status of these days changes depending on the situation of the Jewish people.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written: a formula for explaining a פסוק

phrases.english: As Rav Chana bar Bizna said
that Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Thus said ה׳ of hosts:
The fast of the fourth and the fast of the fifth,
and the fast of the seventh and the fast of the tenth
shall be for the house of Judah for joy and gladness."
It calls them "fast,"
and it calls them "joy and gladness"!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought as support for the discussion right before this section about which fast months need messengers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק gives the same days two opposite labels, fast and joy.

steps.title: It depends on whether there is peace
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא answers: when there is peace these days are joyful, and when there is no peace they are fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there is peace, they will be days of joy and gladness. When there is no peace, they are fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון חסידא solves his own puzzle. The two names in the פסוק describe two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction goes away once you see that the פסוק describes two situations, not one. In times of peace the days turn into celebrations, and without peace they stay fasts.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time when there is peace

phrases.english: At a time when there is peace —
they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is no peace — a fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into two situations: the two labels apply at different times
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seems to contradict itself by calling the days both fasts and joyful days.
steps.terutzMaskana: Peace means joy, and no peace means fast.

steps.title: רב פפא adds a middle situation where fasting is optional
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the פסוק with three situations: peace means joy, persecution means fasting, and neither persecution nor peace means fasting is optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what it means. When there is peace, they are days of joy and gladness. When there is persecution, they are fasts. When there is no persecution and no peace, if people want they fast, and if they want they do not fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sharpens רבי שמעון חסידא's explanation by adding a third, in-between situation. In that situation fasting is a choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון חסידא only described two situations. רב פפא adds a middle one in which fasting is not required. Because the fasts are optional at such times, there is no need to send messengers to tell people the date of those months.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means: a formula that rereads a statement
Persecution: a decree against the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'no peace' automatically means fasting is required. For רב פפא, fasting is required only when there is actual persecution. Without persecution and without peace, it is optional.
steps.whyThisMatters: This three-part rule is the basis for treating these fasts as customs the community accepted on itself, rather than a fixed requirement in every situation.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what it is saying:
At a time when there is peace —
they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is persecution — a fast;
when there is no persecution and no peace —
if they wish, they fast; if they wish, they do not fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines step 2. It answers the unspoken question of why messengers are not sent out for these fast months even when there is no peace.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whenever there is no peace, all four fasts would be required, so messengers should be sent out for each of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without persecution, fasting is optional, so messengers are not needed.

steps.title: Then תשעה באב should be optional too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if so, תשעה באב should also be optional, so why are messengers sent out for אב?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תשעה באב should also be like this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's rule. תשעה באב is one of the four fasts in the פסוק (the 'fast of the fifth'), so it should also be optional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all four fasts follow the same three-part rule, תשעה באב should be optional in quiet times too. But the משנה says messengers go out for the month of אב, which implies its fast is required. The rule seems to clash with the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a challenge built on what was just said

phrases.english: If so, the Ninth of Av also?
phrases.notes: He means: תשעה באב should also be optional, so why does the משנה send messengers for אב?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's three-part rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that the fasts are optional when there is no persecution
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תשעה באב is one of the four fasts, so it should be optional too. Yet messengers are sent out for אב.

steps.title: תשעה באב is different because of its many disasters
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that תשעה באב is different, because many tragedies happened on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: תשעה באב is different, since many disasters happened on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his rule by setting תשעה באב apart as a special case. Its fast stays required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-part rule still holds for the other fasts. תשעה באב is an exception because so many tragedies piled up on that one day, so its fast stays required even in quiet times.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The Ninth of Av is different,
since disasters were multiplied on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁאנֵי תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All four fasts follow the same rule, so תשעה באב should be optional.
steps.terutzMaskana: תשעה באב is an exception because of its many tragedies, so its fast is required.

steps.title: The list of tragedies on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רב פפא by listing the disasters of תשעה באב: both בתי המקדש were destroyed, ביתר was captured, and the city was plowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: On תשעה באב the בית המקדש was destroyed, both the first time and the second, ביתר was captured, and the city was plowed over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב פפא's claim with a known teaching. It lists the many tragedies that happened on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list shows that 'multiplied disasters' is not an exaggeration. Four separate catastrophes fell on one date, and this explains why the day's fast is required and not optional.

keyTerms.meaning: ביתר: a city whose fall ended the בר כוכבא revolt

steps.whatToRemember: The fasts of the fourth, seventh and tenth months depend on the situation: joy in peace, required in persecution, optional in between. תשעה באב stays required because of its many tragedies.

phrases.english: As the Master said:
On the Ninth of Av the Temple was destroyed
the first time and the second,
and Beitar was captured,
and the city was plowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: בְּתִשְׁעָה בְּאָב חָרַב הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim in step 5 that disasters were multiplied on תשעה באב.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that תשעה באב is different
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching listing the tragedies of תשעה באב

steps.title: רבי שמעון introduces four teachings of רבי עקיבא he disagrees with
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון says that רבי עקיבא explained four things in a way that he himself does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון said, רבי עקיבא used to explain four things, and I do not explain them the way he did.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by bringing a ברייתא. This line is a setup: רבי שמעון says he disagrees with four of רבי עקיבא's teachings. Only one of them, about the four fasts in זכריה, is quoted here, and the next steps lay it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this point the גמרא dealt with whether the fasts are required. Now it turns to a different question: which events and dates the four fasts in זכריה stand for. The fast of the fourth month comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: Like him, the way he does

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דּוֹרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva would expound four things,
and I do not expound like him:

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic about the same פסוק in זכריה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי עקיבא on how to explain four things.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the fast of the fourth is the ninth of תמוז
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the 'fast of the fourth' is ט׳ בתמוז, the day the walls of ירושלים were broken through. He proves it from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the fourth' is the ninth of תמוז, when the city was broken into, as it says: 'In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine was strong in the city, there was no bread for the people of the land, and the city was broken into.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא begins explaining the four fasts in זכריה, starting with which day the 'fast of the fourth' stands for. He backs it up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו connects the fourth month and the ninth day with the breaching of the city. So רבי עקיבא dates the fast to ט׳ בתמוז, the actual day of the breach.

keyTerms.meaning: The city was broken into: its walls were breached
As it is said: introduces a proof from a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Today we fast on the 17th of תמוז, not the 9th. Here רבי עקיבא dates the fast by the breach of ירושלים's walls in the days of the first בית המקדש, which the פסוק puts on the 9th.

phrases.english: "The fast of the fourth" — this is the ninth of Tammuz,
on which the city was breached,
as it is stated: "In the fourth, on the ninth of the month,
the famine grew strong in the city,
and there was no bread for the people of the land,
and the city was breached."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבי עקיבא's teaching about the four fasts, which is one of the four teachings announced in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the fourth is ט׳ בתמוז, the day the city was breached.

steps.title: Why is תמוז called the fourth?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the פסוק calls it 'the fourth' and answers that תמוז is the fourth month counting from ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does it call it 'the fourth'? Because it is the fourth of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא clears up a wording question in רבי עקיבא's explanation. 'Fourth' means the fourth month of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'fourth' could seem unclear. The answer is that months are counted from ניסן, so תמוז is the fourth. This confirms that 'the fast of the fourth' points to a day in תמוז.

keyTerms.meaning: Fourth in the order of months

phrases.english: And why does it call it "fourth"?
Fourth of the months.
phrases.notes: Counting from ניסן, the first month, תמוז comes fourth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word in רבי עקיבא's teaching from step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the fast is called 'the fourth'
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמוז is the fourth month counting from ניסן.

steps.title: The fast of the fifth is תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that the 'fast of the fifth' is תשעה באב, when the בית המקדש was burned, and that it is called 'fifth' because אב is the fifth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the fifth' is the ninth of אב, the day the House of our God was burned. Why is it called 'fifth'? Because it falls in the fifth month.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא moves on to the second fast in the פסוק and tells us which day it is. He uses the same pattern as before: name the day, say what happened, then explain the number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the fast of the fourth (Step 9), the number in the פסוק is the number of the month, counting from ניסן. אב is the fifth month, so 'the fifth' means תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the months (in the count of months)

phrases.english: 'The fast of the fifth': this is the ninth of Av,
on which the House of our God was burned.
And why does he call it 'fifth'?
Because it is the fifth of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's list, moving from the fast of the fourth to the fast of the fifth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the fifth is תשעה באב, named for אב being the fifth month.

steps.title: The fast of the seventh is the day גדליה was killed
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the 'fast of the seventh' is ג׳ תשרי, when ישמעאל בן נתניה killed גדליה בן אחיקם. This teaches that the death of צדיקים is as serious as the burning of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the seventh' is the third of תשרי, when גדליה בן אחיקם was killed. Who killed him? ישמעאל בן נתניה. This teaches that the death of צדיקים is equal to the burning of the House of our God. Why is it called 'seventh'? Because תשרי is the seventh month.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains the third fast. He also adds a lesson: a fast was set up for the death of one צדיק, just like for the burning of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fast is not for a building or a city. It is for the killing of one righteous person, and it is treated as seriously as the burning of the בית המקדש. The name 'seventh' again follows the count of months from ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish governor left in ארץ ישראל after the destruction
Is equal to, weighs the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for צום גדליה, and for the idea that losing a צדיק is a loss as great as the burning of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: 'The fast of the seventh': this is the third of Tishrei,
on which Gedaliah son of Ahikam was killed.
And who killed him?
Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed him,
to teach you that the death of the righteous is equal
to the burning of the House of our God.
And why does he call it 'seventh'?
Because it is the seventh of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the third fast and adds a lesson about the death of צדיקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the seventh is ג׳ תשרי, for the killing of גדליה; the death of צדיקים equals the burning of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The fast of the tenth is עשרה בטבת, the start of the siege
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the 'fast of the tenth' is עשרה בטבת, when the king of בבל laid siege to ירושלים, and proves it from a פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the tenth' is the tenth of טבת, when the king of בבל laid siege to ירושלים, as the פסוק says: 'In the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month... the king of בבל laid siege to ירושלים on this very day.' Why is it called 'tenth'? Because טבת is the tenth month.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא explains the last fast on the list and brings a פסוק to show which day it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל gives the exact date, the tenth day of the tenth month, and says the siege began then. So the fast of the tenth is עשרה בטבת, again named by the count of months.

keyTerms.meaning: Laid siege to, closed in on

phrases.english: 'The fast of the tenth': this is the tenth of Tevet,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבּוֹ סָמַךְ מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: on which the king of Babylonia laid siege to Jerusalem,
as it is said: 'And the word of the Lord came to me

phrases.aramaic: בַּשָּׁנָה הַתְּשִׁיעִית בַּחֹדֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי בֶּעָשׂוֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ לֵאמֹר.
phrases.english: in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month, saying:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן אָדָם כְּתׇב לְךָ אֶת שֵׁם הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: Son of man, write down the name of the day,
of this very day:
the king of Babylonia has laid siege to Jerusalem.'
And why does he call it 'tenth'?
Because it is the tenth of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבי עקיבא's list with the fast of the tenth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the tenth is עשרה בטבת, the day the siege of ירושלים began, proven from יחזקאל.

steps.title: Why is the siege listed last if it happened first?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: the siege was the first event, so shouldn't its fast be written first? Why is it written at the end?
steps.simpleTranslation: Wouldn't it have been right to write this one first? Why is it written here?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a problem with רבי עקיבא's reading and sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The siege on עשרה בטבת started the whole chain of disasters. If the fast of the tenth is for the siege, it seems odd that the פסוק names it last instead of first.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי זֶה לִכְתּוֹב רִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: But wouldn't it have been fitting to write this one first?
So why was it written here?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי זֶה לִכְתּוֹב רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the list given רבי עקיבא's reading of the fast of the tenth.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading that the fast of the tenth is for the siege
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The siege happened first in history, so its fast should be listed first, not last.

steps.title: The list follows the order of the months
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק lists the fasts in the order of the months, so the tenth month comes last.
steps.simpleTranslation: In order to arrange the months in their proper order.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is not listing the events in the order they happened. It lists them by month: fourth, fifth, seventh, tenth. So טבת, the tenth month, has to come last even though the siege came first.

phrases.english: In order to arrange the months in their proper order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the order of the list by a different rule (order of months, not order of events)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should follow the order in which the disasters happened.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list follows the order of the months, so the tenth month is last.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the fast of the tenth is ה׳ בטבת, the day the news arrived
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees: the fast of the tenth is ה׳ בטבת, when the exiles in בבל heard the city had fallen. He brings a פסוק from יחזקאל, and says they treated the day of the news like the day of the burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not say so. Rather, 'the fast of the tenth' is the fifth of טבת, when the news reached the exiles that the city had been struck, as the פסוק says: 'In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, a survivor from ירושלים came to me saying: the city has been struck.' And they made the day of the news like the day of the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי שמעון gives his own reading of the fast of the tenth, which is different from רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, the fast of the tenth is not about the siege. It is about the day the exiles in בבל first heard the city had fallen. For them that day felt like the burning itself, so a fast was set on it.

keyTerms.meaning: But I do not say so
The exiles (the Jews living in exile)
The survivor, the one who escaped

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two dates: רבי עקיבא says the fast of the tenth is עשרה בטבת (the siege); רבי שמעון says it is ה׳ בטבת (the news of the destruction).

phrases.english: But I do not say so; rather:
phrases.notes: 'I' here is רבי שמעון, who opened the ברייתא back in Step 7.

phrases.english: 'The fast of the tenth': this is the fifth of Tevet,
on which the news came to the exiles
that the city had been struck,
as it is said: 'And it was in the twelfth year,
in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, of our exile,
the survivor from Jerusalem came to me
saying: The city has been struck.'
And they made the day of the news like the day of the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון rejects רבי עקיבא's reading of the fast of the tenth and offers his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, the fast of the tenth is ה׳ בטבת, the day the news of the destruction reached the exiles.

steps.title: רבי שמעון explains why his reading is better
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues his reading is more convincing: in his view the list follows both the order of the months and the order of the disasters, while רבי עקיבא's reading only follows the order of the months.
steps.simpleTranslation: My words seem better than his words, because I say the first one happened first and the last one happened last, while he says the first one happened last and the last one happened first. He only counts by the order of the months, but I count by the order of the disasters.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a reason why his reading should be preferred over רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי עקיבא's reading, the fast listed last (the siege) was really the first disaster, so the list is out of order in time. In רבי שמעון's reading, the fast listed last (the news arriving) really did happen last, so the list matches both the months and the order of events.

keyTerms.meaning: My words seem more convincing than his

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: the four fasts are listed only by the order of the months, and the fast of the tenth is the siege on עשרה בטבת. רבי שמעון: the fast of the tenth is ה׳ בטבת, the day the news came, so the list also follows the order of the disasters.

phrases.english: And my words seem better than his words,
for I say about the first one that it happened first,
and about the last one that it happened last,
while he says about the first one that it happened last,
and about the last one that it happened first.
phrases.notes: For רבי עקיבא, the siege of עשרה בטבת started everything, yet it is listed last.

phrases.english: But he counts by the order of the months,
while I count by the order of the disasters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון supports his reading from Step 15 by comparing it with רבי עקיבא's answer in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's reading that the fast of the tenth is ה׳ בטבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the list: his reading keeps the fasts in the order the disasters happened, while רבי עקיבא's reading needs the order-of-months answer.

steps.title: Has מגילת תענית been cancelled? Two opinions
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי חנינא say מגילת תענית is cancelled. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב and רבי חנינא say that מגילת תענית has been cancelled. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say that מגילת תענית has not been cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a disagreement between אמוראים: are the special joyful days listed in מגילת תענית still in effect today?
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילת תענית is a list of days that celebrate good things that happened to the Jewish people, and on those days fasting is not allowed. The question is whether these days still count now that the בית המקדש is destroyed. Here the גמרא only states the two opinions; the reasons come next.

keyTerms.meaning: An early list of happy days on which fasting and eulogies are forbidden
It has been cancelled / is no longer in force

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav and Rabbi Chanina say:
Megillat Ta'anit has been cancelled.
phrases.notes: מגילת תענית is a list of happy days when you may not fast.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Megillat Ta'anit has not been cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which date each fast falls on to a new, related question: are the joyful days of מגילת תענית still in force?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: רב and רבי חנינא hold מגילת תענית is cancelled, and רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי hold it is still in force.

steps.title: Why רב and רבי חנינא say it is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק makes the fasts depend on peace. Without peace they are fasts, and the happy days of מגילת תענית also stop without peace.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבי חנינא say מגילת תענית has been cancelled. This is what the פסוק means: when there is peace, these days will be for joy and gladness. When there is no peace, they are fasts. And those days of מגילת תענית are like these: without peace they are cancelled too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of רב and רבי חנינא, using the פסוק in זכריה that the fasts will become days of joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the status of the fast days to whether there is peace. רב and רבי חנינא say the joyful days of מגילת תענית work the same way. When there is no peace, as in the time of גלות, they are not celebrated, so they are cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (explaining a text)

phrases.english: Rav and Rabbi Chanina say
Megillat Ta'anit has been cancelled;
this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק about the four fasts becoming days of joy (זכריה 8:19).

phrases.english: At a time when there is peace,
they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is no peace, a fast.
And those are also like these.
phrases.notes: 'Those' are the happy days of מגילת תענית, and 'these' are the fast days in the פסוק. Both depend on peace.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וְרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמְרִי בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the first opinion in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joyful days, like the fast days, depend on peace. Without peace, the days of מגילת תענית are cancelled.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it still stands
steps.stepSummary: Only the fast days in the פסוק were made to depend on the בית המקדש. The happy days of מגילת תענית stay as they were.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say מגילת תענית has not been cancelled. It is only these fast days that the Merciful One made depend on the building of the בית המקדש. Those other days, the ones in מגילת תענית, stay exactly as they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the second side, רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the פסוק narrowly. It talks only about the four fast days, which change depending on the בית המקדש. Nothing in the פסוק touches the happy days of מגילת תענית, so those days keep their status.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (ה׳, here speaking through the נביא זכריה)
The building of the בית המקדש

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Megillat Ta'anit has not been cancelled:
it is these that the Merciful One made depend
on the building of the Temple,
but those stay just as they were.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי: לֹא בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading of the same פסוק, limiting it to the fast days only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the fast days depend on the בית המקדש. The days of מגילת תענית remain in force.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides read the same פסוק. One side says the happy days of מגילת תענית also depend on peace, so they are cancelled. The other side says only the fast days depend on the בית המקדש, so the happy days still stand.

steps.title: רב כהנא's challenge from a fast decreed on חנוכה
steps.stepSummary: A fast was decreed on חנוכה in לוד. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע protested and told the people to fast again to atone for fasting on that day, so the days of מגילת תענית still count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected: There was a story where they decreed a fast on חנוכה in לוד. רבי אליעזר went down and bathed, and רבי יהושע cut his hair. They said to the people: 'Go and fast another fast to make up for the fact that you fasted on this day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges רב and רבי חנינא with a story about חכמים after the חורבן who would not allow a fast on חנוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנוכה is one of the days listed in מגילת תענית. These events took place after the בית המקדש was destroyed, yet רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע treated fasting on חנוכה as so wrong that the people needed to fast again to atone for it. That suggests the days of מגילת תענית were not cancelled, which goes against רב and רבי חנינא.

keyTerms.meaning: He bathed (something not done on a fast day)

steps.confusionAlert: Bathing and cutting hair here are not random acts. They were public protests, showing the fast should not happen on חנוכה. The second fast was a way of doing תשובה for fasting on a day of joy.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
There was an incident, and they decreed a fast
on Chanukah in Lod,
and Rabbi Eliezer went down and bathed,
and Rabbi Yehoshua cut his hair.
And they said to them:
Go out and fast for the fact that you fasted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the view of רב and רבי חנינא explained in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim of רב and רבי חנינא that מגילת תענית is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After the חורבן, great חכמים still treated fasting on חנוכה (a day in מגילת תענית) as forbidden, to the point of requiring a second fast to atone. So the days of מגילת תענית were still in force.

steps.title: חנוכה is different because it has a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the challenge from לוד. חנוכה is not like the other days of מגילת תענית, because it has its own מצוה of lighting candles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: חנוכה is different, because it has a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled. He explains that the story in לוד proves nothing about the other days, because חנוכה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 20 used חנוכה to prove that all the days of מגילת תענית still count. רב יוסף limits the proof. חנוכה stayed because it has a מצוה attached, so the other days could still be cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different. Used to say a case is an exception.
The eight-day holiday of the Hasmonean victory, listed in מגילת תענית
A commandment. Here it means lighting the חנוכה candles.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Chanukah is different, because there is a מצוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from לוד in step 20 by saying חנוכה is an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to a special case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since people still treat חנוכה as a day you may not fast, all of מגילת תענית must still be in force.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנוכה survived because of its candle-lighting מצוה. The rest of מגילת תענית could still be cancelled.

steps.title: אביי: the מצוה could be cancelled too
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's reason. If the holiday was cancelled, its מצוה could have been cancelled along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let חנוכה be cancelled, and let its מצוה be cancelled together with it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back against רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה exists only because the holiday exists. So having a מצוה is no reason to keep the holiday. If the rabbis cancelled the holiday, the candle-lighting would simply end too.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let it be cancelled, and let its מצוה be cancelled!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's first reason why חנוכה is different
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מצוה depends on the holiday, so it cannot be the reason the holiday stays.

steps.title: חנוכה is different because its miracle is well known
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף changes his answer. חנוכה stays because its miracle is so widely known among the Jewish people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: חנוכה is different, because its miracle is well known.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף drops his first reason and gives a new one for why חנוכה is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason does not depend on the holiday's own rules. It is about how famous the miracle is. A miracle that everyone knows about is not something the rabbis would cancel. So the proof from לוד still does not cover the other days of מגילת תענית.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. Signals a new answer that replaces the old one.
The miracle is well known to everyone

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, even if מגילת תענית was cancelled, חנוכה stays, because its miracle is publicly known.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Chanukah is different, because its miracle is well known.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, שָׁאנֵי חֲנוּכָּה דְּמִיפַּרְסַם נִיסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that was rejected in step 22 with a stronger one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to a special case, for a new reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The candle-lighting מצוה is what kept חנוכה, and אביי showed that this does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the חנוכה miracle is so well known, חנוכה stayed even if the rest of מגילת תענית was cancelled.

steps.title: The holiday of 3 תשרי: God's name in documents
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא begins a challenge by quoting מגילת תענית. On 3 תשרי the practice of writing God's name in documents was ended. The source first explains how that practice started.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא raised an objection: On the third of תשרי, mentioning God's name in documents was cancelled. The Greek kingdom had decreed that the Jews may not say the name of Heaven. When the חשמונאי kingdom grew strong and beat them, they made a rule to mention the name of Heaven even in documents. So they would write: "In year such-and-such of יוחנן the כהן גדול of the God Most High."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It quotes a line from מגילת תענית about 3 תשרי and tells the background story. The actual question comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This challenge targets the view of רב and רבי חנינא in step 17, that מגילת תענית was cancelled. The background matters: the practice of writing God's name in documents began only after the חשמונאים won. So the 3 תשרי holiday was set up fairly late.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection, usually from an older source
The mention, meaning writing God's name
Legal documents, such as loan papers

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna raised an objection:
On the third of Tishrei
the mention was cancelled from documents.
phrases.notes: This is a line from מגילת תענית. "The mention" means writing God's name.

phrases.english: For the Greek kingdom had issued a decree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהַזְכִּיר שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל פִּיהֶם,
phrases.english: not to mention the name of Heaven on their lips.
And when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong and defeated them,
they made a rule that people should mention the name of Heaven
even in documents.
And this is what they would write:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנַת כָּךְ וְכָךְ לְיוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: In year such-and-such of Yochanan the High Priest
of the God Most High.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled, now from a different day.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב and רבי חנינא (step 17) that מגילת תענית was cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the case. The attack itself comes in the next step.

steps.title: A holiday added later proves מגילת תענית was not cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ended the practice of writing God's name in documents, so it would not end up in the garbage, and they made that day a יום טוב. רב אחא בר הונא asks: if מגילת תענית was cancelled, how could they add a new day after cancelling the earlier ones?
steps.simpleTranslation: When the חכמים heard about this, they said: Tomorrow this borrower will pay his debt, and the document will end up thrown on a garbage heap. So they cancelled the practice, and they made that day a יום טוב. Now, if you think מגילת תענית was cancelled, does it make sense that the first days were cancelled and later ones were added?!
steps.whatsHappening: The quote ends with the חכמים cancelling the practice and making the day a holiday. Then רב אחא בר הונא asks his actual question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 3 תשרי holiday was added to מגילת תענית later than the other days. If the whole list had been cancelled, it would make no sense to keep adding new days to it. Adding a new day shows the list was still in force.

keyTerms.meaning: A holiday, here a day when you may not fast
If it enters your mind. Introduces an idea in order to show it is wrong.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up what was cancelled. The practice of writing God's name in documents was cancelled. The day it ended became a new holiday. The question is about adding that new holiday.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a strong challenge to the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled, because here a day was added to it, not just kept.

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard about the matter, they said:
Tomorrow this one will pay his debt,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the borrower. Once the loan is repaid, nobody needs the paper anymore.

phrases.english: and the document will end up thrown on a garbage heap,
so they cancelled them,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the rule about writing God's name in documents.

phrases.english: and that day they made into a holiday.
And if it enters your mind
that Megillat Ta'anit was cancelled,
the first ones were cancelled, and later ones are added?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the quote begun in step 24 and asks the actual question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב and רבי חנינא (step 17) that מגילת תענית was cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A new holiday was added to מגילת תענית later on. That would make no sense if the earlier days had already been cancelled, so the list must still be in force.

steps.title: The new day was added while the Temple still stood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the יום טוב of 3 תשרי was set up while the בית המקדש was standing, before מגילת תענית was cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A time when the בית המקדש was still standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא בר הונא's question from Step 25. It says the new day was added back in the time of the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא בר הונא asked how a new day could be added if מגילת תענית had already been cancelled. The answer is that the order was different: the day was added while the בית המקדש stood, when all of מגילת תענית was still in force. The cancellation came later, only after the חורבן.

keyTerms.meaning: With what are we dealing here? A formula that narrows a source to a specific case

steps.whatToRemember: The days of מגילת תענית were in force, and new ones could be added, while the בית המקדש stood. The cancellation of מגילת תענית refers only to the time after the חורבן.
steps.confusionAlert: There is no contradiction here. Adding the day and cancelling מגילת תענית happened in two different time periods.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
At a time when the Temple was standing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב אחא בר הונא's challenge from Step 25 by placing the added day in the era of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (time-period distinction): the source describes the era before the cancellation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that a new day was added after מגילת תענית had already been cancelled, which would make no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The day was added while the בית המקדש stood, when מגילת תענית was fully in force. The cancellation came only after the חורבן.
